next.reason: 1985: 'An operand is numeric if it consists entirely of the characters 0, 1, 2, 3, ... , 9, with or without an operational sign', refined in the same clause: with no sign in the data description the content must be digits with no sign; with one, digits and a valid sign. §2023:8.8.4.4.4 GR3 n) gives the same test for every 1985 operand: for a numeric display item 'the condition is true if the presence or absence of an operational sign in the content of the data item referenced by identifier-1 is in agreement with the data description of identifier-1' and the rest is digits; for a non-numeric item 'the condition is true if the content ... consists entirely of the characters 0, 1, 2, 3, ..., 9' (1985's unsigned case). The floating-point and other-usage branches cover operands 1985 refused (its DISPLAY-only rule); that widening belongs to the operand rule, not this definition. Same meaning.
